units.title: Construct: Positioned event logs and persistent snapshot roots
steps: Distinguish immutable event history, a current projection, a retained snapshot root and durable storage. Derive why replay requires event-version and external-query assumptions, not merely a list of bytes.

Retain the actual PR-T70-07 learner artifact and its64node/3nodes-per-update contract. Prove16 appends use48nodes, every published root remains immutable and an interrupted failed append cannot advance count. Initialization requires no surviving borrowed roots; do not copy/relocate a live arena and interpret roots in another owner. Account for unpublished cells and allocation counters separately from reachable state. State a release/publication order for a future concurrent adapter.
checks: Append(3,7),append(3,9): prefix1 returns7 and prefix2 returns9. Inject each allocation ordinal1..3 on the next append: count stays2, used count is restored and prior roots still resolve. The17th append returns RP_FULL without consuming nodes.

Separately implement the required codec.records/storage.pages adapter with short writes and crash schedules; the memory anchor does not validate that adapter.

units.title: Construct: CQRS projection admission and atomic position advancement
steps: Separate query-model choice from delivery semantics. Establish exactly-once application only within one serialized projection and one retained immutable log identity; reject the stronger claim of exactly-once external effects.

Prove the invariant count=k implies exactly the first k events contributed once and applied[i].position=i+1. A 16-term int32 sum fits int64 on the declared target. Retain history for conflict checks rather than trusting a reused position from a new log. The caller must associate a projection with one log identity. Explain why a mutex around cursor alone is insufficient, and why an external email/file effect cannot become atomic with this state by naming it CQRS.
checks: Apply(1,0,7) twice yields total7,count1. Reuse position1 with8 conflicts; position3 before2 is a gap. Two synchronized threads each delivering values1..16 yield count16,total136;128 fresh concurrent runs test the adapter.

Run replicated.projection, including actual pthread schedules under GCC TSan when available. Kill duplicate-reapplication and gap-acceptance mutants with semantic assertions. Record mutex boundaries and model the crash point between query-state and cursor persistence. A TSan pass observes these executions only; it does not certify arbitrary effects or all schedules.

units.title: Construct: Lamport, vector and hybrid logical clock boundaries
steps: Derive three different clock contracts: Lamport timestamps preserve happened-before in one direction, vectors characterize causality under fixed known membership, and HLC pairs retain a physical component without eliminating physical-clock assumptions.

Show two concurrent events with ordered Lamport timestamps, two incomparable vectors and every HLC equality case. Separate physical-clock closeness claims from the synchronization assumptions in Corollary1. On local overflow choose explicit failure; neither arbitrary sleep nor silently increasing physical time is equivalent. Outputs are ordinary C structs, so validity and per-replica serialization remain caller obligations.
checks: Lamport(2,8)=9. Vectors[1,0,0] and[0,1,0] are concurrent; receive at replica0 gives[2,1,0]. HLC local(10,2),remote(10,7),wall9 gives(10,8); wall11 on a subsequent local event resets logical to0. UINT32_MAX logical overflow fails unchanged.

Run replicated.clocks and independent exhaustive small HLC branch enumeration plus uint64/uint32 extrema. Kill ignoring-remote Lamport and incorrect equal-physical HLC-counter mutants. Build small message histories and derive causal relations from graph reachability before comparing clock outputs; timestamp ordering alone is not the oracle.
reasoning: Derive three different clock contracts: Lamport timestamps preserve happened-before in one direction, vectors characterize causality under fixed known membership, and HLC pairs retain a physical component without eliminating physical-clock assumptions.
deliverables: Show two concurrent events with ordered Lamport timestamps, two incomparable vectors and every HLC equality case. Separate physical-clock closeness claims from the synchronization assumptions in Corollary1. On local overflow choose explicit failure; neither arbitrary sleep nor silently increasing physical time is equivalent. Outputs are ordinary C structs, so validity and per-replica serialization remain caller obligations.

Run replicated.clocks and independent exhaustive small HLC branch enumeration plus uint64/uint32 extrema. Kill ignoring-remote Lamport and incorrect equal-physical HLC-counter mutants. Change replica membership and persisted restart identities; show why resetting a vector slot or reusing a timestamp identity loses history. units.title: Falsify and transfer: Field tags, minimal varints and canonical bytes
steps: Run replicated.wire and an independent Python parser/encoder for boundary values and reordered field maps. Kill overlong-varint acceptance and incorrect negative ZigZag mutants. Enumerate every truncation, duplicate field, forbidden tag/wire type and output-capacity boundary; demonstrate two noncanonical orders producing the same canonical bytes.

Add length-delimited nested records with depth and total-byte budgets, a critical/advisory negotiation rule and an incremental io.frame decoder. Compare schema migration that retains unknown fields against field-wise reconstruction that loses them. Define canonical NaN/negative-zero/string normalization policy before adding floating or textual values; do not assume the current integer proof extends.

units.title: Construct: Pure reducers, explicit effects and rollback replay
steps: Implement the T20.03 functional-core boundary: explicit state and recorded input produce new state and effect requests, while an adapter owns effects. Demonstrate rollback equivalence without replaying externally visible effects or claiming that ordinary C enforces purity.

Prove determinism from complete state/input and defined unsigned arithmetic. Identify every effect boundary and distinguish speculative requests from committed presentation. Derive rollback of the HAMT used cursor after a failed second update while preserving old reachable roots; staged unreachable arena cells and allocation counters may differ. All arena users must be quiescent during the transaction, and roots from unpublished intermediate updates must never escape. Score overflow or invalid movement must not partially publish a state/effect.
checks: Initial(0,0,0,1),movement-1 gives position15,random1015568748,score0; next movement1 gives position0,score3. Eight inputs[1,1,0,-1,1,0,1,-1] produce score12. Replacing input4 with1 and replaying from the prior snapshot equals a fresh corrected fold. All six checkpoint failure cuts preserve the published root and used count.

Run replicated.replay and exhaustively compare all movement histories of length0..8 with a Python integer model; verify suffix rollback versus full replay. Kill omitted random-score contribution and failed second-update allocation-leak mutants. Build a synthetic effect adapter with idempotency key(timeline,tick) and injected failure; record one duplicate-effect counterexample if replay directly invokes the adapter. Inspect undefined symbols to confirm the core has no time/random/I/O dependency.
